'''Rodney Jay Soward''' (born January 16, 1978) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] and was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the first round of the [[2000 NFL draft]]. Multiple suspensions derailed his career and he was indefinitely suspended by the NFL in 2002. He later played for the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL), with whom he won the [[Grey Cup]].

'''Raleigh McKenzie''' (born February 8, 1963) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] and [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). During a 16-year football career, he played for four different teams. Raleigh played guard for the [[Washington Redskins]] from 1985 to 1994. He was drafted in the 11th round of the [[1985 NFL draft]] by Washington.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1985 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1985/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412043915/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1985/draft.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Nicknamed "'''Rallo'''", he played primarily as a reserve during his first season before becoming a vital starter due to injury. He started in each game after that at any of the five positions on the offensive line, but his speciality was center.  He played on two [[Super Bowl]] champion teams in 1987 and 1991.  He was named to the UPI All-NFL Team in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1991 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1991/allpro.htm |access-date=2023-10-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He also played for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[San Diego Chargers]], and [[Green Bay Packers]].

McKenzie attended [[Austin-East High School]] in Knoxville, where he and his identical twin brother [[Reggie McKenzie (linebacker)|Reggie]] played both at [[linebacker]] and on the offensive line (future Raiders Director of Player Personnel [[Joey Clinkscales]] was among their teammates).  Raleigh was named the 11th-best recruit in Tennessee by the ''[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]'' following his senior year.<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=194&pg=59 1981 Tennessee Signees] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303223739/http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=194&pg=59 |date=March 3, 2016 }}," ''1981 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1981), p. 57.</ref>

The McKenzie brothers played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]] from 1981 to 1984.  Both played linebacker as freshmen, but Raleigh switched to center during his sophomore season.<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=742&pg=52 1982 Tennessee Squad] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303222021/http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=742&pg=52 |date=March 3, 2016 }}," ''1982 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1982), p. 51.</ref>  Playing alongside All-American Bill Mayo and future NFL lineman [[Bruce Wilkerson]],<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=41 1984 Offense] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304084123/http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=41 |date=March 4, 2016 }}," ''1984 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1984), p. 38.</ref> McKenzie anchored a line that helped running back [[Johnnie Jones]] set school records for rushing in 1984.  McKenzie's position coach was future Vol head coach [[Phillip Fulmer]].<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=56 1984 Tennessee Squad] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304094315/http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=56 |date=March 4, 2016 }}," ''1984 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1984), p. 55.</ref> In September 2011, the McKenzie brothers were honored as UT "Legends of the Game" during the Vols' game against [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati]].<ref name="painter" />

McKenzie joined the Redskins for training camp in 2001 assisting the personnel department.  He also ran summer football camp.  Before joining his brother in Oakland, Raleigh was an assistant football coach at [[Herndon High School]] in [[Herndon, Virginia]].<ref name="painter">{{Cite web |last=Painter |first=John |date=September 9, 2011 |title=Catching Up: Raleigh and Reggie McKenzie |url=http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/090911aab.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170607160140/http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/090911aab.html |archive-date=2017-06-07 |access-date=2023-10-09 |website=Tennessee Volunteers Athletics}}</ref> When his brother Reggie was hired as the general manager of the [[Oakland Raiders]], Raleigh joined the team as a scout. After Reggie was fired in late 2018, Raleigh stayed on until after the [[2019 NFL draft]], when new general manager [[Mike Mayock]] announced Raleigh would not be retained.<ref>{{cite web | last=Gehlken | first=Michael | title=Raiders part with scout Raleigh McKenzie, brother of ex-GM | website=Las Vegas Review-Journal | date=2019-05-01 | url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/raiders-nfl/raiders-part-with-scout-raleigh-mckenzie-brother-of-ex-gm-1653262/ | access-date=2025-07-04}}</ref>

Both brothers are members of [[Omega Psi Phi]] fraternity.

'''Raymond Charles Thielemann'''  (born August 12, 1955){{cn|date=June 2025}} is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]]  in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] and the [[Washington Redskins]].

Thielemann played [[college football]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas Razorbacks]]<ref name="hibdon" /> and was selected in the second round of the [[1977 NFL draft]] by the Falcons.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sheeley |first1=Glenn |title=No. 2 Is Most Definitely Not the Falcons' Lucky Number |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-atlanta-constitution-r-c-thieleman/175028118/ |access-date=22 June 2025 |work=The Atlanta Constitution |date=April 28, 1985}}</ref>

At the [[University of Arkansas]], Thielemann helped the Razorbacks to a 10–2 record, win a share of the 1975 Southwest Conference championship, beat the Georgia Bulldogs in the [[1976 Cotton Bowl Classic]] 31–10, and finish ranked No. 7 in the final AP poll. He also was on the [[Super Bowl XXII]] championship [[Washington Redskins]] team in 1987 as a member of the Redskins' famed "[[The Hogs (American football)|Hogs]]" offensive line.

In 1984, Thielemann played in five consecutive games wearing a cast on one hand to protect a broken thumb.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hinton |first1=Ed |title=In This Corner: R. C. Thielemann |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-atlanta-journal-r-c-thielemann/175027920/ |access-date=22 June 2025 |work=The Atlanta Journal |date=November 3, 1984}} </ref> Thielemann was traded to the Redskins for receiver [[Charlie Brown (wide receiver, born 1958)|Charlie Brown]] in 1985.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dunham |first1=Will |title=Redskins Trade Receiver Charlie Brown to Atlanta |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-stuart-news-r-c-thielemann/175028186/ |access-date=22 June 2025 |work=The Stuart News |date=August 27, 1985}}</ref> Later that season he suffered a major knee injury in a game against the Chicago Bears in 1985, but was able to recover and continue playing football.<ref name="hibdon">{{cite news |last1=Hibdon |first1=Glenn |title=Thielemann Eyes Super Bowl Ring for Retirement |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/tulsa-world-r-c-thielemann/175027990/ |access-date=22 June 2025 |work=Tulsa World |date=January 10, 1988}}</ref>
